page: Amazon Web Services c6g.12xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 48 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs of the AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each physical core executes a single thread without hyperthreading, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 96.0 GB, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage or GPU acceleration, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded compute capability and moderate single-threaded throughput. In multi-core CPU testing via stress-ng, the instance achieves a strong score of 72,830.09, landing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower IPC of the Neoverse-N1 core, resulting in lower scores on Geekbench single-core (971.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (20.35 GB/sec). Memory throughput demonstrates 167.78 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 74.87 GB/sec for uncached writes. In application benchmarks, it produces 54.7 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 40.2 GB/sec in static web serving.

Because the server utilizes Graviton Neoverse-N1 silicon, it delivers high physical core density and dedicated thread allocation without simultaneous multithreading overhead, yielding solid compute efficiency across multi-threaded operations. However, workloads requiring high single-core clocks, AVX instruction sets, or substantial per-core memory will experience trade-offs. The c6g.12xlarge is suited for scalable multi-threaded workloads including Clang compilation pipelines, microservices, distributed caching, static web hosting clusters, and batch processing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It supplies 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz with single-threaded execution per core, paired with 96.0 GB of memory for a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage while providing 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core computational throughput, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core result in the top quartile, alongside average memory bandwidth and database operations performance. Single-core throughput is moderate, aligning with the architectural profile of the Neoverse-N1 processor. With its dense core layout and dedicated CPU allocations, c6g.12xlarge is practical for multi-threaded services, batch compute, continuous integration compilation jobs, Redis distributed caching nodes, and parallel web serving architectures.
